contract.direct_answer: Based on general zebrafish eye-development knowledge, the three lineages at 14–24 hpf are canonically distinguished as follows: (1) Periocular neural crest (POM/periocular mesenchyme) — foxc1a/foxc1b, foxd3, pitx2, sox10, eya2, lmx1b, and pdgfra; these cells migrate around the optic cup and give rise to anterior-segment structures. (2) Optic cup (neuroretina/RPE) — rx1/rx2/rx3, vsx2 (chx10), six3, pax6a/pax6b (retinal domain), sox2, and mitfa/otx2 for the RPE layer. (3) Lens placode/lens — pitx3, foxe3, cryaa/cryba/crygamma (crystallins, later), mab21l1, and pax6a/pax6b (shared with retina but with a distinct lens-restricted domain). HOWEVER — I must flag strongly that NONE of these marker assignments are supported by the retrieved evidence bundle. The bundle lists dataset titles (ZESTA atlas CORPUS-2026-0001, anterior-segment scRNA atlas CORPUS-2026-0002) that are HIGHLY relevant and would likely contain exactly this marker information, but no marker-level content, no gene expression tables, and critically no verified ENSDARG identifiers were retrieved. I therefore cannot responsibly assert any ENSDARG. The markers above should be treated as literature-derived hypotheses to be validated against ZESTA/anterior-segment atlas data and ZFIN, not as evidence-grounded findings from this bundle.
